panels.title: Packed input construction
panels.contract: Complete Boolean output; fully charged resident requests
panels.scope: Windows; fresh synthetic confirmation; all seven backend paths
panels.note: The shared packed-mask constructor benefits direct BitSet and CSE too. Original bars are an explicit ablation, not a current backend. Warm results and regressions remain available.

panels.title: Cache reuse and changing names
panels.contract: Repeated complete-output requests with bounded retained masks
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 7702P; consumed portability panel; 2 MiB cache / 64 KiB pressure case
panels.note: Same-basis reuse, changing names, phases and pressure are separate cases. A gain on renamed inputs does not establish a default cache policy.

panels.title: Complete output delivered to a file
panels.contract: Parse, prepare, deliver all bytes, flush/fsync, close and verify
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 7702P; fresh synthetic n22/n24 outputs; q1/q8
panels.note: Every arm pays the same file-delivery obligations. Small chunks and warm batches can regress. No measured chunk size was installed as a default.

panels.title: Counts from independent components
panels.contract: Exact scalar count; no complete output requested
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 7702P; fresh synthetic AND components and OR fallback control
panels.note: The entangled1 identifier is an OR root that this AND-only plan does not decompose. The separate factorized and bucket panels test broader mechanisms; do not mix their timings across hosts.

panels.title: Fresh-process peak memory
panels.contract: Process high-water mark including interpreter and libraries
panels.scope: Separate Linux EPYC 7713 memory diagnostic; three fresh children per method
panels.note: This later /proc VmHWM diagnostic supersedes the equal inherited-rusage counters in the earlier file run. Its host differs from the timing panel; it is not a latency comparison.

panels.title: Factorized OR, XOR and mixed counts
panels.contract: Exact scalar counts through expression or CM ingress
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 7713; development n12/n16 and confirmation n22/n24
panels.note: All three CUDD orders and the inseparable-cycle regression are retained. The cycle has a later bucket-mechanism comparison on its own host; this panel measures the factorized implementation.

panels.title: Current affine counts and native control
panels.contract: Exact count after fixed assignments; packed-row ingress
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 7713; eight public coding matrices and fresh n1024/n2048 controls
panels.note: The current indexed Python and indexed M4RI arms are compared on the same host. Original versions are labelled ablation controls. These final values supersede the earlier unindexed timings; no dense-FLINT ratio is presented as a general native win.

panels.title: Overlapping CNF constraints: Python, arrays and CUDD
panels.contract: Exact counts over every declared CNF variable; not projected feature products
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 9654; all 35 final-panel cases; q1/q8; nine paired repetitions
panels.note: Ten of eleven admitted full public CNFs fit the bucket limits. All resource refusals are shown without zero-height bars. Arrays help larger factors but lose on many narrow cases; both natural and dynamic CUDD remain strong controls. Public inputs in this follow-up are reused diagnostics.

panels.title: Current bucket and native process memory
panels.contract: Fresh child process high-water mark; q1
panels.scope: Linux EPYC 9654; three children per method and selected case
panels.note: These values include interpreter and import costs. Refused plans are labelled and are not ranked as successful low-memory counters. Reused-service and simultaneous-query memory need separate measurement.

panels.title: Completed native batch gate
panels.contract: Sum of fully charged case medians, not one request latency
panels.scope: Windows; independently frozen prospective workload; q8/q32/q96
panels.note: The q96 gain is below its frozen 1.10× materiality requirement. The candidate is a completed no-go for this workload; the earlier functional-only status is superseded. No learned router is promoted.

panels.title: Distinct projected assignments
panels.contract: Exact integer answers for the unchanged 32-request trace; full and projected contracts are separate.
panels.scope: Linux CPU; latest same-machine replay of the declared development and confirmation cases; nine repetitions
panels.note: Count each selected-variable assignment once, including when auxiliaries have multiple witnesses. Full counts are a separate selectable contract. The natural-order native control is faster on the tested independent-auxiliary and adjacent-exclusion families; hidden-star projection is explicitly refused by all three bucket variants. No general native-performance advantage is established.

panels.title: Additional full and projected CNF cases
panels.contract: Exact integer answers for the unchanged 32-request trace; full and projected contracts are separate.
panels.scope: Additional public systems; latest isolated-method diagnostic on consumed inputs; nine repetitions where complete
panels.note: Whole DIMACS files and unchanged 32-request traces. Projection selects even-position declared variables; this is not claimed to reconstruct original feature-product semantics. Each measured method has its own process and 120-second limit. If the independent oracle times out, the methods are explicitly marked not measured. The earlier harness stopped a whole case when one competing native control failed; these diagnostic reruns preserve failed/refused methods and carry no paired comparative confidence claim.

panels.title: A separate pipe consumer
panels.contract: Producer and reader verify the same full output or cancelled prefix.
panels.scope: Linux CPU; producer plus separate OS-pipe reader; nine fresh-process repetitions
panels.note: The reader checks every delivered byte. Slow-reader cases wait 0.5 ms after each up-to-4-KiB read. Cancellation is checked between chunks; a full-output chunk completes before it can stop. First-reader time is the return of the first read, not the arrival of its first byte. Memory is the sum of separate lifetime peak RSS measurements, an upper bound rather than simultaneous RSS. No durable-storage claim.

panels.title: Preparation and retained-plan reuse
panels.contract: Checked inert JSON reload recompiles; no compiled-plan persistence is claimed.
panels.scope: Linux CPU; four structural inputs and 1/32/256 requests; nine repetitions
panels.note: Fresh compilation starts with an existing expression. Checked reload includes file read, SHA-256 check, JSON validation and compilation. Resident-call timing excludes original construction; the second metric adds its separately recorded construction. Initial fsync storage costs are in the download. Reload did not beat fresh compilation; reuse requires a useful plan lifetime.

frontiers.independent_note: Nine prospectively selected public instances from three application families; six declare projection sets. Each admitted case used three fresh-process repetitions per method, eight generated contexts, 30-second worker deadlines and declared resource limits. No independent exact count comparison completed, so diagnostic timings and integers in the download establish no speedup or accepted output-count claim.
frontiers.mapping_note: Original XML feature identities determine the selected variables. SAT miters are checked by Glucose3 and Minisat22. Original-feature configurations and concrete-feature selections are separate contracts; abstract features are not guessed encoding auxiliaries. Ubuntu and Windows explicitly eliminate every assignment of two and six unmatched CNF variables. One extended feature format remains refused.

consumer.note: An opt-in local recorder is implemented for the maintained video compiler. Operator intent and call return are insufficient to admit a natural-use trace; independent provenance and downstream use still need review.
